title: His records and favorite trumpet players
summary: He owns 30 or 40 LPs and blends Bunk Johnson, Bix and King Oliver. He likes Johnny Wiggs and thinks of Emmett Hardy, who Conner says never recorded.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: Well, do you have many records yourself?

Uh, I, I have, uh, I guess I have about 30 or 40 records of my own, you know. And, uh, I think most of the stuff I might have learned right off those records, you know, listening to the records and just pick it up.

LPs. You see, uh, well, like I said before, uh, I like Bunk Johnson. I like Big Spider-Bank. I like King Oliver. So what I do is try to combine all that three styles together and maybe I'll come up with one of my own, who knows.
I like to play their stuff, you know. Any other trumpet players you can think of from your records?
Uh, I like, uh, I like Johnny Wigg. I like the way Johnny Wigg plays. He has a simple pure style. I like that. Uh, he, uh, let's see, I'm trying to think of this, this other, was it Emmett Hardy?
He sounds pretty much like a, a recording I have of Emmett Hardy. Their stuff sounds pretty much the same, you know, and I like that. I like that, that style.
I don't think you have a record of Emmett Hardy. Was it Emmett Hardy? I don't think he made any records I've ever issued.
You know? Well, I might be wrong. I'm a, maybe, maybe it's something I'd overheard that their styles were... Yeah. I'm pretty sure, I'm pretty sure it's, uh, it's something on Emmett Hardy.
You got me thinking, um, I have to think about it.
Yeah. If you got an Emmett Hardy record, let me know. It should be worth a couple of thousand at least. Well good, I'll sell it. It could be though, you know, those things turn up.
It's just like a, like a bowling recording. They tell me that's worth a little money if you can find one, huh? Yeah. Did he ever do any recording? Supposed to have.
Even Hardy made home recordings and nobody could find them. Buddy Petit made home recordings.
